reasons.heading: Your Dentistry is Strong. But Your Visibility Isn’t
reasons.body: Most dentists build their practice on skill and referrals. Without digital marketing for dentists that works, patients judge them online on profiles, reviews and response speed, often before meeting them.
points: Patients can’t find you by name — searching your name shows a directory listing or a thin profile, not your practice.
Your expertise stays invisible — your implant or orthodontic training isn’t on your website, so patients choose a bigger-looking clinic.
Calls go unanswered mid-procedure — while you’re treating a patient, new enquiries ring out and book with someone else.
Directories control your bookings — Practo and Justdial bring enquiries, but show competing clinics right beside your listing.
High-value cases need more trust — implant and aligner patients want to hear from the dentist first, and find nothing to watch or read.
Advertising rules feel unclear — unsure what dental ethics rules allow, many dentists avoid marketing, or take risks without knowing.
No time to manage marketing — between treating patients and running the practice, marketing becomes irregular and hard to judge.

faqs.q: What is digital marketing for dentists?
faqs.a: Digital marketing for dentists, also called dental digital marketing, uses Google Ads, Google Maps, SEO, social media and WhatsApp to help patients find, trust and book a dental practice. Done well, it is measured by patients seen and cost per patient, not by clicks.

faqs.q: Should dentists market themselves or their clinic?
faqs.a: Market the practice, with the dentist as its trusted face. India’s dental ethics rules limit self-promotion, so profiles should share factual qualifications, experience and treatments. Educational videos and pages build personal trust without breaking the rules or relying on claims.

faqs.q: Is Practo enough, or do dentists need their own website?
faqs.a: Practo and directories help patients discover you, but you don’t control the listing, the reviews or the competing clinics shown beside you. Your own website and Google Business Profile let patients book you directly, and keep your reputation in one place.

faqs.q: How should dentists respond to negative Google reviews?
faqs.a: Reply calmly within a day, thank the reviewer and offer to discuss the issue privately. Never mention treatment details or confirm the person was your patient. A professional reply often reassures future patients more than the original complaint worries them.

faqs.q: What does digital marketing for dentists cost in India?
faqs.a: Dental Google Ads leads typically cost ₹120 to ₹250 in Tier-2 cities, ₹180 to ₹320 in Hyderabad, ₹220 to ₹400 in Bangalore and ₹280 to ₹500 in Mumbai. Your total budget depends on treatments, competition and how many patients you can see.

faqs.q: How long before a new dental practice gets patients from Google?
faqs.a: Google Ads can bring enquiries within weeks of launch, with useful data in 30 to 45 days. A new Google Business Profile usually gains visibility in 60 to 90 days, while organic rankings for treatment searches build from month four onwards.
